solves: Gives an application its command menus in a horizontal bar, such as File, Edit and View: each top item opens a panel with the commands of its subject, by click or by keyboard, following the menubar pattern of the APG.
use_when: For an application with many commands that group into a few subjects, such as a document editor, a spreadsheet or a drawing tool, used with keyboard and mouse.
In the header of the application, always in view, with each panel opening by click or by keyboard.
A shortcut at the end of the item, to teach the keyboard to whoever uses the mouse.
A choice of the item (single or multiple) for display options, such as a ruler, a grid or a density.
narrow when the width of the page does not hold the bar: the application swaps the bar for the button with the bars icon.
do_not_use_when: To go to another page: use nph-navigation-menu or nph-sidebar.
For the frequent actions that must stay in view: use nph-toolbar.
For the few actions of one button: use nph-dropdown-menu.
For the actions of the object under the pointer: use nph-context-menu.
As a bar with a single top item: the bar groups subjects, and one subject is a button that opens a menu.
With a submenu inside a submenu: one level only; what goes beyond goes to a dialog.

menus.constraint: Property only. The top items, in order. A menu is { value, label, disabled, items }: value and label are required, label is the text of the top item, already localized and preferably one word, and items are the entries of its panel. The entries are an item (type absent or item), a label (type label, with text) that names the group after it, and a separator (type separator) that closes a group. The fields of an item are in the business rules. Two menus, or two items of a menu, with the same value leave the second one out. A list that is not a list, with no valid menu, or a menu with no valid item, draws nothing and emits console.error in development, one per cause.

open-menu.constraint: The value of the menu whose panel is open; empty is closed. The bar writes it when the person opens or closes a panel; the consumer may set it to show a panel open, and a panel opened from code takes no focus. A value that names no menu is reported in development and cleared; one that names a disabled menu is cleared. A menu that sits in the overflow item is not shown open by this property, since only the person opens the overflow item. It is ignored while narrow. Opening and closing fire no event.

open-submenu.constraint: The value of the item whose submenu is open; empty is closed. The bar writes it when the person opens or closes a submenu; the consumer may set it to show the submenu open. A value that names no enabled item with a submenu in the open panel is reported in development and cleared. A closed bar has no submenu open.

label.constraint: The accessible name of the bar, already localized, such as Editor menu: the menubar role asks for one. It wins over the aria-label of the host. A bar with neither draws and warns once in development, since the name may arrive after the first render.

more-label.constraint: The text of the overflow top item, already localized, such as More. The bar measures itself and puts the top items that do not fit into that last item. Empty: nothing overflows into a menu, and the piece warns once in development.

narrow.constraint: The consumer swaps the bar for the button with the bars icon, which opens one panel with the menus as items with a submenu. The consumer chooses it, since the width is the page to know: the piece does not measure the breakpoint, by the rule of narrow of nph-navigation-menu. It needs menu-label, and without it the piece draws nothing and emits console.error in development. Reflects so the consumer can style and check the state.

menu-label.constraint: The accessible name of the narrow button, already localized, such as Menu. Required when narrow, because the icon has no text. Not read when the bar is wide.

bar.choose_when: Closed (the Figma `aberto` `não`) is the bar alone; open (`sim`) is the bar with the first top item open and its panel below. The piece draws both from open-menu.

top_item.choose_when: default at rest; hover and open share one look (the Figma `hover-aberto`); focus (`foco`) for keyboard users; disabled on a menu that does not apply now.
do_not_combine_with: a disabled bar: there is no such property; a bar that does not apply on a screen leaves the screen.

submenu.choose_when: closed by default. An item with a submenu draws the arrow and carries no shortcut. The submenu opens to the right of the panel, on the line of its item, at dropdown/submenu-offset, and to the left only when there is no room on the right.
do_not_combine_with: a shortcut or a choice on the same item: the arrow takes the end of the item.
a second level: a submenu has one level only.

width.choose_when: Wide when the bar fits the page, with the overflow item holding what does not fit; narrow on a narrow screen, chosen by the consumer.

size.choose_when: not_applicable. The top item is control/height-default high and the panel item 36; there is no compact size.

hover_open.changes_for_user: The top item takes the primary surface and its text. The pointer over it and its open panel share this look.

focus.token: border border/width in focus/border, radius focus/border-radius-control; halo focus/ring-width in focus/halo, radius focus/radius-control-with-border; no background
focus.changes_for_user: For keyboard users, a border and a halo outside the top item.

disabled.changes_for_user: The whole top item loses opacity; no hover. It takes the focus but does not open.

open_and_focus.token: pending: the look is not drawn in Figma. The code composes the two accepted looks: the background and the label of hover_open plus the border and the halo of focus
open_and_focus.changes_for_user: While the arrows switch menus, the focus stays on the open top item, so it shows both looks (D-1, answered on 26/11/2026).

business_rules: A menu has value, label, optionally disabled, and items. An item has value and text, both required, and optionally icon, severity, selection, checked, shortcut, submenu and disabled. An invalid entry is left out, with one console.error per cause in development.

An item with a submenu takes no selection and no shortcut, and its submenu holds at least one valid item and no submenu of its own. A label entry opens a group and names it; a separator entry closes the group; a group with no item is dropped, and its separator goes to the next group.

The bar has one Tab stop, on the top item used last (the first one, the first time): Tab enters and leaves the bar. With a panel open, Tab closes it and leaves. A click on a top item opens its panel; a click on the open one closes it. With a panel open, the pointer over another top item switches to it.

The first panel opens below its top item, aligned with the start of the item, at menubar/panel-offset; it turns up when there is no room below, moves sideways past the side edge and shrinks and scrolls when it is short of height. The collision padding to the window edge is 4 px, a code setting with no token.

The submenu opens to the right of the item, with its first item on the same line as the item that opened it, and to the left only when there is no room on the right. A gap of dropdown/submenu-offset (4 px) separates the panel from the submenu, on the side that faces the panel; the code reads the token from the computed style. In right-to-left writing everything mirrors, and Left and Right swap.

When the person activates an item, the bar fires nph-item-select, which bubbles, with detail value, checked and menu: checked is the new state of a single or multiple choice and null on a common item; menu is the value of the top item the command belongs to, also from the overflow panel and from the narrow button. A single choice already checked fires again with checked true. Changing menus, open-menu or open-submenu from code fires nothing.

After an activation, the bar replaces menus with a new list that carries the new checked, also inside a submenu; the objects of the consumer are never changed. Single choice is exclusive inside its group.

Enter on an item activates it and closes the whole menu, also on a checkbox and a radio. Space on a checkbox or a radio checks it without closing; on a common item, it does the same as Enter. A click on a common item or a single choice closes the menu; on a multiple choice it keeps it open. An item with a submenu opens its submenu when activated. Focus goes back to the top item when the menu closes by an item or Esc.

Esc closes one level at a time: the first closes the submenu and focuses the item that opened it, the second closes the panel and focuses the top item. With the panel closed, on the top item, Esc does nothing. A press outside closes the panels and leaves the focus where the person pressed; a press on another top item switches menus.
A disabled top item or panel item takes the focus and does not run (aria-disabled). Hide an action the person can never perform (permission); disable one that is unavailable now.

Overflow: the bar measures its own width. The top items that do not fit go into a last top item, with more-label as its text, which opens a panel with them as items with a submenu, in one level. The bar does not wrap into a second line. A menu that already has a submenu shows those items under a group label, so the panel stays in one level. Without more-label nothing overflows.

narrow: the consumer swaps the bar for a button with the bars icon, named by menu-label, which opens the same panel as the overflow item, with every menu as an item with a submenu in one level. The piece does not measure the breakpoint. Mobile is out of this piece.
The panel is not an instance of nph-dropdown-menu in code: it is drawn by the bar, with the same dropdown/* tokens, so it looks the same (D-4).

The panel enters and leaves with motion/enter-* and motion/exit-*, sliding space/inline-tight. Under reduced motion, opacity only, on motion/hover-duration. A submenu opens and closes by pointer after motion/hover-delay.
ai_hints: Use nph-menubar for the commands of a whole application, grouped by subject; for frequent actions in view, use nph-toolbar; for the few actions of one button, use nph-dropdown-menu; for the actions of an object, use nph-context-menu; to go to another page, use nph-navigation-menu or nph-sidebar.
Give the bar its name with label, and fill menus with data: each menu has a value, a label and items, with labels and separators between the groups.
Listen to nph-item-select on the bar and read detail.value, detail.checked and detail.menu.
Show the shortcut at the end of the item, and use a single or multiple choice for display options, because the mark shows the state besides the color.
Leave a command that does not apply now disabled, not hidden, and put the destructive item last, after a separator, with an icon and a label that say the action.
Give more-label so the top items that do not fit go into the last item, and choose narrow, with menu-label, when the page is narrow: the piece does not measure the breakpoint.
Do not nest a second submenu, and do not put a shortcut or a choice on an item with a submenu.

accessibility.semantics: The bar is role=menubar, named by label. Each top item is a native button with role=menuitem, aria-haspopup=menu and aria-expanded. The panel is a popover in the top layer with role=menu named by its top item; every group is a role=group, named by its label when it has one, because the separator is hidden from the accessibility tree. A common item is menuitem; a single choice is menuitemradio; a multiple choice is menuitemcheckbox; aria-checked follows checked. An item with a submenu carries aria-haspopup=menu, aria-expanded and aria-controls, and the submenu is a menu named by that item. The inner nph-checkbox is inert: the item carries the role, the state and the focus. The overflow item is a menuitem with aria-haspopup inside the bar.
accessibility.accessible_name: The bar: label, else the aria-label of the host. A top item: its label. An item: its text, through aria-labelledby. The shortcut goes in aria-keyshortcuts, written in the syntax of the attribute (Ctrl becomes Control, the Command symbol becomes Meta). The narrow button: menu-label. Icons, box, arrow and check are not read.
keyboard: Tab and Shift+Tab: one stop in the bar, on the top item used last; with a panel open, they close it and leave the bar.
On the bar, with the menu closed: Left and Right move between the top items with wrap, and Home and End go to the first and the last (the two arrows swap in right-to-left).
Enter, Space and Down on a top item open its panel on the first item; Up opens it on the last item.
With a panel open, Left and Right close it, move to the neighbor top item and open its panel, keeping the focus on that top item.
In the panel: Down and Up move with wrap; Home and End go to the ends; a typed character goes to the next item that starts with it.

Right opens the submenu of an item that has one and focuses its first item; on an item with none, it goes to the next menu. Left closes the submenu and gives the focus back to its item; at the first level it goes to the previous menu.
Enter activates the item and closes the menu, also on a checkbox and a radio; Space checks a checkbox or a radio without closing, and on a common item does the same as Enter.
Esc closes one level at a time: the submenu, then the panel, giving the focus back to the item that opened it; on the top item with the menu closed, it does nothing.
accessibility.focus: On the top item: keyboard only, a border of border/width in focus/border and a halo in focus/halo outside the item; the border carries the focus, the halo is decorative. In the panel the item takes the same border in focus/border, and the halo. Opened by keyboard, the first item takes the focus and shows it; opened by a click, it takes the focus without showing it. The pointer over a panel item takes the focus to it. When the menu closes, the focus goes back to the top item.
accessibility.contrast: The top item label passes 4.5:1 in both themes: menubar/trigger-foreground on color/background at rest and, in hover or open, menubar/trigger-foreground-hover on menubar/trigger-background-hover, with the lowest at 6.43:1 across the seven brands and the two themes. The focus/border border of the top item passes 3:1 on color/background in every brand, the lowest 4.32:1 (light, Comercial); the halo is decoration. The focus/border border of the panel item passes 3:1 on color/popover in every brand and both themes (Gerencial, dark: 5.53:1). The text of the panel comes from the dropdown item; its lowest is 5.2:1 (checked radio, Financeiro, dark). A disabled item is outside the rule.
accessibility.color_alternative: The open top item has the open panel below it, besides the background. The item with a submenu has the arrow, and open it keeps the hover background. A checked checkbox shows the check in the box and a checked radio shows the check at the end of the item. The destructive item says the action in its label and carries the trash icon, besides the color.

invalid_combinations: menus that is not a list, or with no valid menu — there is nothing to open; the bar draws nothing.
a menu without value, label or a valid item — it has no name, no text or an empty panel; the menu is left out.
two menus, or two items of a menu, with the same value — the event could not tell them apart; the second one is left out.
an item without value or text — it has no name or nothing to report; the item is left out.
submenu with a selection other than none — a submenu item is not a choice; the item is left out.
submenu with a shortcut — the arrow takes the end of the item; the item is left out.
an item inside a submenu that has a submenu — one level only; the item is left out.
narrow without menu-label — the button has an icon and no text; the bar draws nothing.
anti_patterns: Using the bar to go to another page: use nph-navigation-menu or nph-sidebar.
Using the bar for the actions of one object or one button: use nph-context-menu or nph-dropdown-menu.
Making a bar with a single top item.
Nesting a second level of submenu.
Putting the destructive item among the other actions.
Hiding a command that does not apply now, instead of disabling it.
Making the bar the only path to a command that people need in view: the toolbar keeps it in view.
